articles.title: Breville Eye Q toaster review: a ‘revolutionary device’ that makes perfect toast without me trying
articles.summary: I toasted just about every kind of bread in Breville’s new Eye Q – and each slice came out perfectly toasted. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things. It’s a centuries-old problem: how to prepare the perfect slice of toast.
body: The core technology of the toaster has changed little in the past 100 years. A coil of high-resistance wires is activated for a certain period, and the radiant heat from that coil warms and browns the bread. The only measure of doneness that a traditional toaster has is time, but, as anyone who has had burnt toast for breakfast knows, time is a very imprecise proxy.

Breville’s new Eye Q toaster aims to change that legacy. Rather than setting a clock to tick until toast pops out, the Eye Q actually “looks” inside the toaster at the bread to determine whether it is done, thanks to a heat-resistant optical sensor that flashes 10 times per second to monitor the browning process. Hence the gadget’s catch phrase: “We watch your toast so you don’t have to.”

“It took us 10 years to get this project right,” Tom Groundes-Peace, global category manager and head of research at Breville, said. Groundes-Peace likens the innovation to the electric car: while cars evolved over the last century, they were all variations powered by an internal combustion engine. Until the electric motor.

articles.title: ‘I love the boldness of modernism’: New York fashion week goes highbrow
articles.summary: Georgia O’Keeffe inspires the latest Calvin Klein while Michael Kors feels indebted to Alexander Calder. Calvin Klein has taken a highbrow turn in the two years since Veronica Leoni took charge.
body: Leoni called this the “discipline of removal”. Her muse this season was Georgia O’Keeffe, an artist who the brand’s namesake founder admired. Klein bought O’Keeffe’s painting Summer Days in 1983 for $1m, subsequently donating it to the Whitney Museum. A checked pattern taken from O’Keeffe’s distinctive capsule wardrobe of utilitarian chic appeared on this catwalk as a wrap coat, hardware-free with a fabric belt and no buttons.

One nod to pop culture was allowed: a model in a crepe-back satin ivory slip dress, her blond hair scraped back by a simple headband, called to mind the late Carolyn Bessette-Kennedy, the iconic Calvin Klein employee who was launched back into the fashion conversation by Ryan Murphy’s Love Story earlier this year.

Over at the Michael Kors show staged in the sunny courtyard of the Museum of Modern Art, the first model was wearing glossy black disc earrings the size of potato crisps suspended from glinting stainless steel hooks. They looked like pieces from Alexander Calder’s huge mobile, Lobster Trap and Fish Tail, which hangs in the stairwell of the museum.

articles.title: Calvin Klein and Rosalía Celebrated the Return of Euphoria over Jell-o-Shots at People’s
articles.summary: Calvin Klein and Calvin Klein Fragrances celebrated the launch of the new iteration of Euphoria with a post-show cocktail party at People's, featuring a special appearance by campaign star Rosalía.
body: For the fashion set—and now, almost everyone, thanks to the popularity of Ryan Murphy’s Love Story —1990s-era Calvin Klein conjures images of Carolyn Bessette-Kennedy, pencil skirts, and white orchids. Mid-2000s Calvin Klein, on the other hand, brings to mind one particular citrusy and exotic scent, housed in a sexy bottle, and with a sexy ad series to match. Who didn’t have or want Euphoria on their vanity, back then? Even a whiff of it smells like a night out before cell phones: indiscriminately androgynous and intoxicating—or as one Reddit user called it, “almost narcotic.”

As of now, Euphoria is so back —with a new, more intense and potent concentration and a slick campaign fronted by Rosalía (gone are the muscled male models and oiled chests of yore, it seems.) Moments after the Calvin Klein Collection runway show on Friday, the Grammy-winner and recent Vogue cover star said that Euphoria always reminds her of singing on stage or being behind the wheel of her car—two moments that make her feel euphoric.

articles.title: Deepfakes are wrecking influencers’ credibility, one fake ad at a time
articles.summary: Influencers aren’t just battling competitors for brand deals. They’re now battling AI versions of themselves. Earlier this year, Emily Schuman, the creator of the lifestyle blog Cupcakes and Cashmere, saw a photo of herself she didn’t recognize on Instagram.
body: The ad was based on a digitally altered version of a selfie Schuman had taken in her car and posted on Instagram years earlier. Once her followers got wind, they flooded her inbox with questions about the sponsorship as it didn’t seem consistent with Schuman’s personal brand. Soon after, Schuman discovered this was just the beginning. There was also an Instagram post where an AI version of her with darker hair appears to apply foundation to promote a makeup brand called Meroda Cosmetics, and TikTok posts with generated images of her promoting the blood testing company Superpower.
“It’s so violating,” she said. The videos and images look “just like me, but the upside down version”.

Neither Gala nor Meroda responded to requests for comment. Superpower CEO Max Marchione said the TikTok post wasn’t a real ad, but instead came from a scammer his company later reported. “Whilst scamming isn’t new, AI has made this much worse,” he said.

articles.title: ‘The balloons made me smile but his expression made me stop’: Harivansh Verma’s best phone picture
articles.summary: While celebrating a religious festival on the banks of the Ganges, the Indian photographer captured the everyday struggle of a street vendor. It had been a sacred day for Harivansh Verma. It was the evening of Ganga Dussehra, the major Hindu celebration and gathering along the banks of the Ganges.
body: “Haridwar holds a lot of deeply spiritual memories for me and my family,” Verma says. “In Hinduism we believe taking a dip in the Ganges cleanses you of your sins. Devotees travel from across the country and the ritual baths go on continuously from sunrise until late into the night. The atmosphere is magnificent.”

It was early evening when Verma took a stroll along the shore, looking for moments to capture with his smartphone. “When I came across this young man, the balloons made me smile at first, but his expression is what made me stop.”

Verma didn’t know the man, and they exchanged few words, aside from asking permission to take the shot. “There was nothing out of the ordinary about him, but his expression clearly reflected the heavy weight of worry and responsibility he was carrying. The contrast between the exhausted look on his face and the cheerful smiley faces on the balloons felt like two completely different stories existing in one frame.”
Verma hopes people will have a similar experience looking at this image. “Maybe they’ll smile at first, but then spend a little longer looking at him and wondering about his story.”

articles.title: From Melania to Michelle: The 9/11 Memorial Ceremonies and Somber FLOTUS Fashion
articles.summary: Current and former first ladies of the United States gathered at ceremonies in Virginia and New York to commemorate the 25th anniversary of the terrorist attacks.
body: Yesterday, ceremonies were held across the country to commemorate the 25th anniversary of the September 11 terrorist attacks. America’s current and former first ladies gathered at memorial services in New York and Virginia, where their clothing was, understandably, subdued. But even within the traditional tones of black, brown, navy, and gray, each woman remained distinctly herself.

At the Pentagon in Arlington, Virginia, FLOTUS Melania Trump joined President Donald Trump for a service in the courtyard. The first lady wore a slate-gray Dolce & Gabbana suit: a single-breasted wool Turlington blazer with coordinating palazzo pants and a pointed-collar black shirt underneath. It was structured and sharp—a silhouette that has become something of a signature for Mrs. Trump, particularly at major public events.

Dolce & Gabbana, too, is familiar territory. Mrs. Trump has repeatedly turned to the Italian house for significant appearances, making its exacting tailoring and polished finish part of her broader visual vocabulary. On Friday, those codes were pared back even further, the muted palette and precise proportions meeting the gravity of the occasion.

articles.title: 11 National Parks That Are Even More Beautiful in the Fall
articles.summary: Enjoy changing leaves in Shenandoah and cooler days in Big Bend.
body: I’ve traveled far and wide through America’s national parks, and if there’s one thing I’ve learned, it’s that some landscapes are simply better with a little fall color. Come September and October, sweeping valleys turn gold, forests flare in riots of red and pops of orange, and high country trails welcome that crisp, exhilarating drop in temperature that makes you want to keep trekking a little farther. Even parks we know and love in summer feel completely transformed: the sunsets shine differently, wildlife activity changes, and the seasonal crowds begin to give way to a quieter, more immersive experience.

Thanks to the breadth of terrain across the US national parks, there’s no single version of how to experience fall. You might be leaf-peeping beneath the peaks of the Tetons, winding through Acadia’s brilliant coastal forests, hiking Yosemite in the cooler weather, or watching the aspens flicker across the Rockies. And when the sun goes down, the day doesn’t have to end: there are campfires to linger around, stars to seek out, and hot springs to slip into.

articles.title: Newport, Rhode Island, Is New England’s Gilded Jewel—Here’s Where to Eat, Stay, and Play
articles.summary: Consider this your guide to Rhode Island's historic haven by the sea.
body: Newport, Rhode Island, has certainly been having a moment as of late. You can attribute it to the Gilded Age dramas taking over small screens, the old-money aesthetic taking over TikTok, the Real Housewives of Rhode Island taking over Bravo, or just the fact that it’s beyond beautiful all year long. Either way, it’s undeniable that this compact coastal city has become a mecca of sorts for travelers eager to live out their East Coast fantasies—seafood, seersucker, sailboats, and all.

But truth be told, Newport has never been a bad idea. The charming city has been a popular summer destination since the early 19th century, first as a playground for America’s elite, with families like the Vanderbilts and Astors building massive mansions along the water to serve as vacation homes (more on those later). Today, it’s a little less exclusive and a hot spot year-round, with New Englanders and international visitors alike spending sunny days becoming one with the sand at Easton’s Beach, breezy afternoons hiking the Cliff Walk, and chilly nights imbibing their way through Bowen’s Wharf before retreating to shingled cottages and luxurious hotels across town.
